neutral_facts.value: The accused, along with his uncle and aunt, were charged with kidnapping, rape, and murder of a minor girl. The prosecution alleged that the accused kidnapped the girl and raped her, while the uncle and aunt concealed her in their house. The girl was found dead in the accused's residence. The accused and the girl were found to have attempted suicide together, with the girl dying. The accused's attempt to commit suicide was noted. The girl's suicide note stated that she left her home by her own free will and committed suicide, which led to the acquittal of the accused on charges of kidnapping, rape, and murder. The prosecution's case relied on the presumption that the accused had kidnapped the girl based on her being found in his residence, but this presumption was deemed misconceived.

key_evidence_accepted.value: The Supreme Court accepted the 'suicide note' written by the deceased Sushila as key evidence, which indicated that she had left her residence by her own free will and committed suicide.

quotes.text: The 'suicide note' of Sushila is available on the record of this case as annexure P-6. The aforesaid 'suicide note' was produced as exhibit 'DE' before the trial Court. The same is extracted hereunder

witness_credibility.value: The court assessed the main witnesses, including the deceased's family, and found that the prosecution failed to produce any other evidence to demonstrate that the appellant had enticed the deceased or forced her into any act.

quotes.text: In view of the clear and unequivocal statement made by the deceased Sushila to the effect, that she had left her residence by her own free will, it was not possible to record the guilt of the appellant under Section 363 of the Indian Penal Code. This, on account of the acknowledgment, that no other evidence had been produced by the prosecution, to demonstrate that Sat Parkash had enticed the deceased Sushila, to accompany him.

appeal_history.value: Trial court: Acquittal of uncle and aunt; conviction of appellant; High Court: Upheld the order of conviction; Supreme Court: Allowed the appeal and set aside the conviction

quotes.text: The trial court acquitted uncle and aunt of all offences - Appellant was acquitted of offence of murder and convicted u/ss.363, 366, 366-A, 368, 376 - High Court upheld the order of conviction - In the instant appeal, appellant is challenging the conviction order by placing reliance on the 'suicide note' stated to have been written by the deceased

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the appellant kidnapped a minor girl and raped her, with his uncle and aunt helping to conceal her, leading to her murder by administering poison.

quotes.text: Prosecution case was that appellant kidnapped a minor girl and raped her - His uncle and aunt knowing about the kidnapping helped him in concealing the girl in their house and they all in furtherance of common intention committed murder by administering poison to her

defence_argument.value: The defence relied on the 'suicide note' written by the deceased, stating that she had left her residence by her own free will and committed suicide, not being forced or compelled to marry the appellant.

quotes.text: In the suicide note, deceased had made unequivocal statement to the effect that she had left her residence by her own free will - It was, therefore, not possible to record the guilt of appellant u/s. 363

legal_principle_applied.value: The court applied the principle that the prosecution must establish the guilt of the accused beyond a reasonable doubt, and that the suicide note provided a clear and unequivocal statement of the deceased's intent.

quotes.text: It is not in dispute that appellant had also made a similar attempt to commit suicide along with the deceased - In the suicide note, deceased had made unequivocal statement to the effect that she had left her residence by her own free will
